definition.code:
def _mark_asset_blocked(conn, cur, run_id: str, chart_id, asset_id: str, blocking_deps: list[str]) -> None:
    """
    Mark an asset BLOCKED because an upstream it depends on errored/was blocked.

    Recorded as state='error' (the loud, surfaced state — red in the tracker, counted in
    the run's error tally) with a 'BLOCKED:' message, rather than silently running the
    writer on incomplete upstream data and marking it 'complete'. The asset is NOT executed.
    """
    msg = (
        "BLOCKED: upstream dependency(ies) %s did not complete in this run; "
        "skipped to avoid building on incomplete data"
        % ", ".join(sorted(blocking_deps))
    )
    _mark_asset_error_terminal(conn, cur, run_id, chart_id, asset_id, msg)
    logger.warning("[orchestrator] BLOCKED %s — upstream not complete: %s", asset_id, blocking_deps)

recommendation.carrier: disposition='blocked_dependency' (already provisioned) for the WHY, plus a NEW COLUMN for the root/immediate-cause asset id. Do NOT add a new `state` value.
reasoning: A3's own precedent (runner.py:539-561, _terminalize_diverged_assets docstring, 'F-3 rereview') already ruled on this exact question: a cascade victim is deliberately reported via the SAME state='error' used for a genuine cause — 'reported as a genuine FAILURE ... not a cancellation, which is the stronger and more accurate signal for an operator to act on' — specifically so existing state='error'-keyed monitoring keeps matching. Introducing a new `state` value (e.g. 'blocked') would break that continuity and would ALSO require a CHECK-constraint migration on a column two other subsystems (deriveState.ts, AssetNode.tsx, the watchdog reaper) already pattern-match against by literal value.

disposition='blocked_dependency' is additive and free: the enum slot already exists, so setting it costs zero migration. It lets every consumer keep treating state='error' as 'this run did not succeed' (unchanged operator semantics) while giving code that wants to differentiate a cause from a cascade a clean boolean-ish signal (disposition = 'blocked_dependency' vs NULL/'build') without touching the state machine.

A brand-new column (e.g. build_run_assets.blocked_by_asset_id text, nullable) is needed regardless of the disposition choice, because NEITHER table has any structured place for 'which asset id caused this' today — that fact is currently only recoverable (partially) by regex-parsing the `error` prose, which is exactly the fragility this packet exists to fix.

asset_throughput does not need a matching disposition column: it already stays state='error' (unchanged), and any caller wanting the cause/cascade distinction for the CURRENT state of an asset should join out to that asset's most recent build_run_assets row for the same reason build_run_assets, not asset_throughput, already carries 'skip_no_delta'/'build' disposition today.

breakdown_of_the_1236_by_mechanism.meaning: 1,183 rows genuinely name one or more real upstream asset_id(s) as the blocker. 53 rows are actually THIS asset's OWN writer_timeout_seconds expiry (execute_dag line 673) forced through the same 'BLOCKED: upstream dependency(ies) <X> did not complete' text template with the synthetic non-asset-id string 'timeout:600s' standing in for a dependency name. These 53 are NOT cascade victims at all — they are themselves root causes wearing cascade-victim prose. Backfilling them as disposition='blocked_dependency' would be actively WRONG (inventing a false cascade attribution the engine never asserted); they should be excluded from any backfill and, prospectively, should never route through _mark_asset_blocked() at all — a distinct code path/message is needed for a self-timeout.

chain_depth_of_the_1183_genuine_rows.methodology: Parsed each row's error text (regexp to extract the comma-joined dependency id list), exploded it to one row per named blocking asset_id, then LEFT JOINed each named id back into build_run_assets on the SAME run_id to see whether the NAMED blocker is itself a genuine root failure, itself ALSO a cascade victim (another BLOCKED: row), or absent from the run entirely.
chain_depth_of_the_1183_genuine_rows.query_summary: 3 buckets over the exploded dependency-edge set (2,856 edges from 1,183 rows, since many rows name more than one blocking dep):
chain_depth_of_the_1183_genuine_rows.meaning: 89% of the blocking-dependency mentions point to ANOTHER blocked (not-root) asset in the same run. The stored text captures only the IMMEDIATE upstream, never the transitive root — exactly the gap this packet exists to close. Recovering a true root_asset_id from history requires a recursive self-join walk per row (mechanically possible within a single run_id, since the text reliably names real asset_ids for the non-timeout rows), but it was never designed or stored as such, and for 88 of the 2,856 edges (3%) the named blocker does not even appear as a row in that run's build_run_assets at all (most plausibly a cross-scope/global asset referenced by the deadlock branch at runner.py:653, whose own state lives only in asset_throughput, not in this run's build_run_assets set) — for those, no root is recoverable from build_run_assets alone under any amount of text-walking.

6_backfill_question.can_the_root_be_recovered_from_text_alon: Only PARTIALLY, and only via a nontrivial, undocumented, multi-hop reconstruction that the engine never performed or stored as a decision — not a straightforward backfill. For the 1,183 genuine rows: a same-run recursive walk resolves ~97% of the individual dependency-edges (223 direct + 2,545 resolvable-by-further-walking) to SOME row in the run, but walking to a true terminal root requires following potentially several hops per BLOCKED row, and 3% of edges dead-end with no corresponding row at all. For the 53 timeout rows: the 'root cause' IS the row itself, not anything in its own blocking_deps text — but the text actively misdescribes it as a dependency block, so a naive backfill parser would misattribute even these 53 as cascade victims of a fictitious upstream named 'timeout:600s'.
6_backfill_question.verdict: B1 should be PROSPECTIVE-ONLY for the new root-cause column. A coarse RECLASSIFICATION of the 1,236 historical rows' disposition (state='error' + error LIKE 'BLOCKED:%' + NOT the timeout pattern -> disposition='blocked_dependency') is honest and defensible, because it restates something already true in the stored text without inventing anything. But populating a single, specific root_asset_id column for those same historical rows would require either (a) an expensive, never-before-run multi-hop graph reconstruction whose result the engine did not originally assert and which fails outright for 3% of edges, or (b) inventing/guessing — both of which the campaign's 'never invent data' constraint and CLAUDE.md §N.7 item 6 ('an honest null beats an invented judgment') rule out as a backfill. The 53 timeout rows must be excluded from ANY blocked_dependency backfill entirely — reclassifying them would assert a false cascade relationship the code never computed.

mechanism.finding: All 7 anomalies carry the TIMEOUT-mislabeled text (section 6), never a genuine dependency-name text. Their (run_id, asset_id) primary-key row was first written to state='error' by _mark_asset_error_terminal (execute_dag's timeout branch, runner.py:673), then LATER overwritten to state='complete' by a subsequent successful write to the SAME (run_id, asset_id) — most plausibly a retry/resume path that reuses the original run_id per asset (asset_runner.py has four distinct 'UPDATE build_run_assets SET state = \'complete\' ...' statements: lines 644, 992, 1065, 1370). NONE of these four statements clears the `error` column — each is a bare SET state=... (plus ended_at / disposition in two of them), leaving whatever prose the earlier timeout-block write had stamped there untouched.
mechanism.corroborating_asymmetry: The parallel success-path writes to asset_throughput DO clear the equivalent field: e.g. asset_runner.py:637-641 sets 'last_error = NULL' in the same success block that writes build_run_assets state='complete' at line 644 without clearing build_run_assets.error. This is a real, narrow, pre-existing bug: build_run_assets' own success-path writes forgot the error-clear that asset_throughput's parallel writes remembered.
mechanism.why_governance_missed_it: platform/scripts/governance/ekv_controls.py's F-102 control (lines 358-395) already checks for exactly this defect CLASS ('an earned completion state sitting beside a value that denies it') but only against asset_throughput.state IN ('lit','mature') — it does not check build_run_assets.state='complete', so it does not and cannot catch this specific instance.

does_B1_make_this_better_worse_or_unaffe.verdict: UNAFFECTED AT BEST, WORSE IF DONE CARELESSLY.
reasoning: B1's stated scope (separate blocked-from-failed at the source; disposition/root-cause carrier; surface fixes) does not touch the four state='complete' UPDATE statements in asset_runner.py that fail to clear `error` — that is a distinct, pre-existing defect (an orphaned success-path write), not the cause/cascade conflation B1 targets. Fixing B1 alone leaves this stale-error-text bug exactly as-is.

If B1 is implemented CORRECTLY — i.e. it recognizes the timeout branch (runner.py:673) as a distinct mechanism from a genuine dependency block and does NOT tag it disposition='blocked_dependency' (per the section 6 verdict) — these 7 rows are UNAFFECTED: they still show state='complete' with a stale (and still slightly misleading, 'upstream dependency(ies) timeout:600s') error string, exactly as today, but at least B1 introduces no NEW false signal on them.

If B1 is implemented carelessly — i.e. any future code path pattern-matches on the literal 'BLOCKED:' prefix (live or as part of a backfill) without excluding the timeout branch — it would ALSO stamp disposition='blocked_dependency' onto these 7 already-contradictory rows (state='complete' + would-be disposition='blocked_dependency' is a strictly worse, newly self-contradictory combination than today's state='complete' + stale prose). B1's implementation must explicitly special-case/exclude the timeout branch text from whatever pattern or code path assigns the new disposition/column.
